title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: August 1, 2026 – Major signings, key injuries, and coaching carousel continues.

items.headline: Draymond Green Officially Re-Signs with Warriors
items.summary: Veteran forward Draymond Green has officially inked a new one-year deal worth $27.7 million to remain with the Golden State Warriors. The four-time NBA champion and All-Star extends his tenure in the Bay Area, adding a crucial piece to their core.

items.headline: Spanish League MVP Mario Hezonja Returns to NBA, Signs with Cavs
items.summary: Former No. 5 overall pick Mario Hezonja is making his NBA comeback, signing a one-year deal with the Cleveland Cavaliers. The 31-year-old Croatian, who was the Spanish League MVP last season with Real Madrid, averaged 13.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 2.4 assists.

items.headline: Wizards' Jamir Watkins Suffers Torn ACL, Likely Out for 2026-27 Season
items.summary: Washington Wizards young wing Jamir Watkins will likely miss the entire upcoming 2026-27 season after suffering a torn ACL in his left knee during the NBA Summer League opener. The 25-year-old underwent surgery on Thursday to repair the injury.

items.headline: Nic Claxton Traded to Chicago Bulls
items.summary: Center Nic Claxton has been moved to the Chicago Bulls in a deal that was largely a footnote to the trade sending LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Claxton's addition is seen as a significant move for the Bulls' frontcourt depth.

items.headline: 76ers Trade Johni Broome to LA Clippers
items.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers have traded forward Johni Broome and a second-round pick to the LA Clippers in exchange for cash considerations. The deal was officially announced on Tuesday, July 28th.

items.headline: Hawks Acquire Luguent Dort in Three-Team Deal
items.summary: The Atlanta Hawks officially acquired guard Luguent Dort from the Oklahoma City Thunder in a three-team trade, which also involved Zaccharie Risacher heading to the Dallas Mavericks. The deal provides the Hawks with a strong defensive presence.

items.headline: LeBron James Signs with Philadelphia 76ers
items.summary: In one of the offseason's biggest bombshells, four-time MVP LeBron James has officially signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers, teaming up with newly acquired Jaylen Brown. This move marks James' 24th NBA season.

items.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo Joins Miami Heat
items.summary: Two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo made a monumental move this offseason, joining the Miami Heat. This trade reshapes the Eastern Conference landscape, setting up a new rivalry with LeBron James.

items.headline: Marcus Smart Inks Two-Year Deal with Houston Rockets
items.summary: Guard Marcus Smart has agreed to a two-year, $13 million contract with the Houston Rockets, including a player option for the second season. The former Defensive Player of the Year adds depth and a veteran defensive presence to the Rockets' backcourt.

items.headline: Ricky Rubio Extends Deal with Joventut Badalona
items.summary: Veteran guard Ricky Rubio will remain with Joventut Badalona for the 2026-27 season, having signed a one-year contract extension. This marks his second consecutive season with the club after returning from the NBA.

items.headline: Golden State Warriors Crowned 2026 NBA Summer League Champions
items.summary: The Golden State Warriors defeated the Memphis Grizzlies to claim the 2026 NBA Summer League Championship. The tournament concluded on Sunday, July 26, after weeks of intense competition in Las Vegas.

items.headline: NBA Cancels Abu Dhabi Preseason Games Amid Geopolitical Conflict
items.summary: The NBA will reportedly not hold preseason games in the Middle East ahead of the 2026-27 season. The league decided against staging games in the region due to ongoing conflict involving the United States and Iran.

items.headline: Offseason Coaching Carousel Continues with Key Hires
items.summary: The offseason has seen several significant coaching changes: Tiago Splitter (Chicago Bulls), Dusty May (Dallas Mavericks), Taylor Jenkins (Milwaukee Bucks), Jamahl Mosley (New Orleans Pelicans), Sean Sweeney (Orlando Magic), and Micah Nori (Portland Trail Blazers) have all been hired as head coaches. Dave Joerger also joined the Denver Nuggets as lead assistant.

items.headline: Former Spartans Jaxon Kohler and Tre Holloman Granted Extra College Eligibility
items.summary: A federal court judge in Colorado has granted a primary injunction, allowing college athletes who graduated high school in 2022 an extra year of eligibility. This ruling could see former Michigan State players Jaxon Kohler (Utah Jazz Exhibit 10 contract) and Tre Holloman (Orlando Magic Summer League) return to college, despite their recent professional participation.
